topic: Very long working weeks are linked to stroke
subject: society

sources.title: Long working hours and risk of coronary heart disease and stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis of published and unpublished data for 603 838 individuals
Long Working Hours and Coronary Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
The association between long working hours and health: A systematic review of epidemiological evidence
Long Working Hours and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease
The Effect of Long Working Hours and Overtime on Occupational Health: A Meta-Analysis of Evidence from 1998 to 2018
Long working hours as a risk factor for atrial fibrillation: a multi-cohort study

facts.claim: Employees who work long hours have a higher risk of stroke than those working standard hours.
facts.quote: Employees who work long hours have a higher risk of stroke than those working standard hours; the association with coronary heart disease is weaker.

facts.claim: Long working hours are linked to a 1.21-fold (95% CI 1.01-1.45) increased risk of stroke.
facts.quote: Our meta-analytic update of summary evidence suggests a 1.12-fold (95% CI 1.03-1.21) increased risk associated with coronary heart disease and a 1.21-fold (95% CI 1.01-1.45) increased risk of stroke

facts.claim: Long working hours are linked to an overall odds ratio of 1.245 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.195-1.298) for occupational health.
facts.quote: The overall odds ratio between long working hours and occupational health was 1.245 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.195-1.298).

facts.claim: Long working hours are linked to significant adverse effects on all-cause mortality, circulatory disease, diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, depressive state, anxiety, other psychological disorders, sleep condition, cognitive function, and health-related behavior.
facts.quote: Long working hours had significant adverse effects on most health outcomes.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

rejected.claim: Working long hours is linked to a 4-fold increased risk of atrial fibrillation compared with those working standard hours.
rejected.quote: 4-fold increased risk of atrial fibrillation compared with those working standard hours (hazard ratio = 1. 42, 95% CI = 1. 13-1. 80, P = 0. 003).

research.angle: Working long hours is linked to an increased risk of stroke and atrial fibrillation, as well as various other adverse health outcomes.
research.verdict: The evidence consistently links long working hours to increased risks of stroke, atrial fibrillation, and broader occupational health issues.
research.caveat: The evidence for cardiovascular risk is described as somewhat inconsistent, with some studies showing a small risk and others showing larger effects.
